-122.26620,37.81170.name: Spring Fertility-East Bay
-122.26620,37.81170.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Thomas E. Fisher, DO. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-72.31936,43.64884.name: White River Junction VA Medical Center
-72.31936,43.64884.state: WHITE RIVER JUNCTION, VT, UNITED STATES
-72.31936,43.64884.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Department of Veterans Affairs. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

174.76000,-36.85300.name: Fonterra
174.76000,-36.85300.desc: A New Zealand dairy cooperative, one of the largest dairy exporters in the world, owned by its farmers. New Zealand permits no GM cultivation, and its export position depends partly on that status — which makes the country’s restriction a commercial asset as well as a policy.

-77.09700,38.98800.name: Newborn screening and residual dried blood spots
-77.09700,38.98800.desc: Nearly every baby born in the United States has blood taken for screening, and the leftover cards have been retained by state laboratories for years — used for research, and in some cases subpoenaed. Texas and Michigan were both sued over it. A universal public health programme is also the largest unconsented biobank in existence.

9.50000,51.34000.name: TÜV, DEKRA, DNV, LRQA and the rest of the certification field
9.50000,51.34000.desc: Beyond the firms with their own entries here, published surveys of food certification name DEKRA SE, DNV, ALS Limited, TÜV SÜD, Lloyd's Register, Kiwa, NSF International, Socotec, Aspirata in South Africa, and Indocert, TQ Cert and MS Certification Services in India. The TÜV organisations show the scale involved: TÜV Nord alone, founded 1869, employs more than 15,000 people in over 100 countries. Their certification lines cover food safety, organic, quality management, gluten-free, halal, kosher, non-GMO, fair trade and sustainability — non-GMO certification is one product in a catalogue sold to manufacturers, retailers, restaurants, caterers and agricultural producers. The per-country resources on this map name national certifiers; this is the field they sit in.
